learning_outcomes.title: Special-product factorization
learning_outcomes.statement: Factor binomials that are differences of squares and factor perfect square trinomials.
learning_outcomes.rule_summary: A² − B² = (A − B)(A + B). A² ± 2AB + B² = (A ± B)². Extract the GCF before applying a special-product pattern.

questions.title: A • Difference of squares
questions.stem: Factor over the integers and justify every stage.

parts.prompt: Factor 12x² − 75y² completely. Show the GCF and the difference-of-squares step.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: 12x²−75y² = 3(4x²−25y²) = 3(2x−5y)(2x+5y). Award 1 for GCF, 1 for squares, 2 for factors.
18a⁴−50a² = 2a²(9a²−25) = 2a²(3a−5)(3a+5). Award 2 for GCF and 2 for binomial factors.

parts.prompt: Expand one of your factorizations to verify it.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: For example, 3(2x−5y)(2x+5y)=3(4x²−25y²)=12x²−75y². Award 2 for valid expansion.

questions.title: B • Perfect square or near miss?
questions.stem: Use the middle-term test, including the sign.

parts.prompt: Show that 9t² − 30t + 25 is a perfect square trinomial and factor it.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: 9t²=(3t)², 25=5², and −30t=−2(3t)(5). The factorization is (3t−5)². One mark for each check/factor stage.

parts.prompt: Determine whether 4c² + 12cd + 9d² is a perfect square trinomial. Justify and factor.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: Yes. 12cd=2(2c)(3d), so the factorization is (2c+3d)². Award 2 for test and 1 for factors.

parts.prompt: A student claims 4c² + 10cd + 9d² = (2c + 3d)². Explain the error.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: (2c+3d)² has middle term 12cd, not 10cd. Award 1 for expansion fact and 1 for conclusion.

parts.prompt: Find k so that x² − 18x + k is a perfect square.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: k=(18/2)²=81. Award 1 for method and 1 for value.

questions.title: C • Dimensions and repeated factoring
questions.stem: A rectangular panel has area 4x² − 100 square units, with x > 5.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: 4(x²−25)=4(x−5)(x+5). Award 1 for GCF and 2 for difference-of-squares factors.

parts.prompt: Give possible positive length and width expressions and verify their product.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: Possible dimensions are 2x−10 and 2x+10. Their product is 4x²−100. Both are positive for x>5. Award 3.

parts.prompt: If x = 8, find those dimensions and the area.

answer.model_answer_and_marking: At x=8 the dimensions are 6 and 26, and area=156. Award 2.
